feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: ESMA Sets 2027 Priorities to Strengthen, Simplify and Integrate EU Capital Markets
entry.summary: ESMA sets 2027 priorities for stronger, simpler and more integrated EU capital markets ESMA · Sep 28, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU financial markets regulator, published its 2027 Annual Work Programme on 28 September 2026. Guided by its 2023–2028 strategy, the programme shifts several major initiatives from preparation to delivery. Key areas include simplifying regulatory and reporting frameworks, expanding supervisory mandates such as for ESG rating providers, and greater use of data and technology in supervision.

entry.title: ESMA recommends changes to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging crypto services
entry.summary: ESMA calls for changes to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging services ESMA · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has responded to the European Commission's public consultation on reviewing the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). Its recommendations cover stronger investor protection, such as stricter marketing rules and cost transparency for staking, lending and borrowing, enhanced supervisory powers, clearer rules for decentralised finance and token classification, and simplification of the framework, alongside a pathway toward tokenised capital markets.

entry.title: ESMA clarifies EU market access to third-country CSD services
entry.summary: ESMA clarifies access for EU market participants to the services of third-country CSDs ESMA · Oct 7, 2026 ESMA has issued a statement saying EU market participants should not be blocked from third-country Central Securities Depositories after the transitional regime ends on 17 January 2027, until EU legislation extending it is finalised. The Council and European Parliament both support the extension under the Market Integration and Supervision Package. ESMA expects national competent authorities not to prioritise supervisory or enforcement action against unrecognised third-country CSDs until the extension takes effect.

entry.title: ESMA sets supervisory expectations for services linked to non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins
entry.summary: ESMA sets out supervisory expectations on services related to unauthorised stablecoins ESMA · Oct 8, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has issued an opinion clarifying its supervisory expectations for crypto-asset services involving asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens, known as stablecoins, that do not comply with MiCA. It states that MiCA-authorised crypto-asset service providers should stop providing such services to EU clients. National competent authorities should require remediation of any remaining exposures no later than three months after publication.

entry.title: ESMA seeks evidence on using tokenised collateral in central clearing
entry.summary: ESMA seeks evidence on the use of tokenised collateral in central clearing ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has launched a Call for Evidence on whether EU central counterparties (CCPs) could safely use tokenised collateral, with responses due by 15 January 2027. The paper examines how tokenisation may affect the transfer, management, protection and use of collateral across its lifecycle, including after a clearing member default. ESMA will assess the feedback in the first quarter of 2027.

entry.title: Carlo Comporti named new Chair of ESMA
entry.summary: Carlo Comporti appointed Chair of the European Securities and Markets Authority ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has announced that Carlo Comporti has been appointed as its next Chair, confirmed by the Council of the European Union. He takes up the position on 1 November 2026. Current Chair Verena Ross welcomed him and reflected on her five years leading the authority. Comporti previously served as a Commissioner at Italy's CONSOB and as a member of ESMA's Board of Supervisors and Management Board.

entry.title: ESMA Appoints Carlos San Basilio to Its Management Board
entry.summary: ESMA appoints Carlos San Basilio as the new member of its Management Board ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority has appointed Carlos San Basilio of Spain's CNMV as a new member of its Management Board. He replaces Carlo Comporti of Italy's CONSOB, who steps down to become ESMA Chair effective 1 November. The election took place at the Board of Supervisors meeting in Paris on 6 October 2026. The Management Board, chaired by the ESMA Chair, ensures the Authority fulfils its mission under its founding Regulation.

entry.title: ESMA publishes thematic notes on clearer impact and transition sustainability claims
entry.summary: ESMA promotes clarity in claims on impact and transition ESMA · Oct 12, 2026 ESMA has published two thematic notes on sustainability-related claims, covering positive impact claims made through funds and bonds and climate transition claims. Based on observed market practices, they offer do's and don'ts with examples to help make communications clear, fair and not misleading, reducing greenwashing risk. The notes do not create new regulatory requirements or prescribe a particular approach.

entry.title: ESMA Sets Out 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities for Listed Issuers' Annual Reports
entry.summary: ESMA sets out 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities ESMA · Oct 13, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority has published its 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities for annual financial reports of issuers on EEA regulated markets. Focus areas include geopolitical risks and restructuring provisions in IFRS financial statements, materiality assessment and connected information in ESRS sustainability statements, and common errors in the statement of changes in equity under ESEF. ESMA also published the 31st extract from its FRWG (EECS) enforcement database, containing seven decisions on IFRS and APM Guidelines.

entry.title: EU supervisors publish 2027 work priorities
entry.summary: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027 ESMA · Oct 13, 2026 · Crypto The Joint Committee of the EBA, EIOPA and ESMA published its 2027 Annual Work Programme, setting out priorities for cross-sectoral risks and coordination. Key areas include digital operational resilience (under DORA, including oversight of critical ICT third-party providers), technological innovation, sustainable finance, securitisation and risk monitoring. The programme also covers consumer protection and supports the EU's simplification agenda to reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens.

entry.title: ESMA analysis finds cross-border investment services kept growing in 2025
entry.summary: ESMA analysis shows continued growth in cross-border investment services ESMA · Oct 14, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), together with national competent authorities, has published its annual analysis of cross-border investment services provided to retail clients across 30 EU/EEA jurisdictions. It finds 379 firms served retail clients cross-border in 2025, with about 15.5 million clients receiving services from firms in other Member States, almost twice the 2023 figure.

entry.title: ESMA's third sanctions report calls for more consistent enforcement across the EU
entry.summary: ESMA's third Sanctions Report highlights the need for greater convergence in enforcement ESMA · Oct 15, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has published its consolidated report on sanctions and measures imposed across the EEA in 2025. National authorities imposed more than 950 administrative sanctions and measures, with administrative fines totaling almost €82 million, and settlements were used more often. The report finds significant differences in enforcement and says ESMA will foster exchanges among national authorities so similar breaches lead to similar outcomes.

entry.title: ESMA updates transparency manual with guidance on OTC derivatives and tick-size regime
entry.summary: ESMA updates its manual on transparency with new guidance for OTC derivatives and tick-size regime ESMA · Oct 15, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has updated its manual on pre- and post-trade transparency under MiFID II/MiFIR. The update clarifies which over-the-counter derivatives are subject to transparency requirements, how their identifying reference data should be provided, and adds Q&As and recommendations on the tick-size regime. The updated manual is to be considered a draft until the related technical standards (RTS 2 and the RTS on CTP input/output data) enter into force.

entry.title: One year before EU T+1 settlement: rules are complete, market players must now prepare
entry.summary: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 The EU will move to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. ESMA has published revised guidelines on standardised procedures and messaging protocols, clarifying new requirements for allocations and confirmations that apply from 7 December 2026. ESMA urges market participants to finalise technical preparations, assess readiness across their ecosystems and begin testing throughout the trading and settlement chain as soon as possible.

entry.title: ESMA finalises revised guidance on delaying disclosure of inside information
entry.summary: ESMA finalises the review of guidelines on the delay in disclosure of inside information ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has updated and streamlined its MAR guidelines on delaying the public disclosure of inside information. The guidelines add five further legitimate interests that may justify a delay, such as a public authority's request for confidentiality. Legitimate interests tied to protracted processes were removed because issuers no longer must disclose such information before those processes finish. The revised guidelines apply from their publication on ESMA's website in all 24 EU official languages.

entry.title: New Q&As published on crowdfunding, crypto-asset and clearing rules
entry.summary: New Q&As available ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 · Crypto ESMA has published new Q&As covering European crowdfunding service providers, the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), and the EMIR framework for OTC derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories. Three CCP-related questions are listed: the AAR 85% exemption, AAR thresholds calculation, and the AAR representativeness obligation.

entry.title: ESMA sets requirements for safe use of post-trade risk reduction services
entry.summary: ESMA specifies requirements to facilitate safe use of post-trade risk reduction services ESMA · Oct 20, 2026 ESMA's final report sets out the conditions providers and users of post-trade risk reduction (PTRR) services must meet for certain OTC derivatives to be exempt from the EMIR 3 clearing obligation. It also establishes safeguards for providing these services and monitoring use of the exemption. The rules build on existing market practice and aim to avoid unnecessary additional requirements.

entry.title: ESMA trims outdated and duplicative market structure Q&As under simplification drive
entry.summary: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts ESMA · Oct 22, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority has updated its Q&As on market structure under MiFID II, MAR and the Short Selling Regulation. As part of its Simplification and Burden Reduction initiative, it withdrew or amended guidance that is outdated, duplicative or covered by other ESMA publications. The aim is to reduce complexity and keep the Q&As consistent with the current legislative framework.
